ops: A term of service, a contract, an indenture, or a charter made under the Commonwealth’s law is not, in the Church’s teaching, a sale. The woman is not traded, her soul is not conveyed, and she returns to her keeping when the term ends. The Church leaves the form, the limits, and the penalties of every such instrument to the Commonwealth. The Church’s censure falls where a soul is sold, and the Commonwealth’s law governs everything else.

ops: The Commonwealth’s law of the Darlorath is civil law, made by the Crown and Parliament and adjudicated by the Magistracy. Article IV states canon and is neither its source nor its limit. The Crown and Parliament may pass and amend this law, and the Magistracy rules on it, without reference to the Holy Synod.

ops:
Matter | Rule
Source | Crown and Parliament; adjudicated by the Magistracy. Canon is the Church’s and does not bind the state
The Darlorath | The master’s dominion over the woman: her person, her labor, her obedience, her silence, her body, and her bearing, in the full weight of civil law. One man holds it, and none holds it in common
Title | Passes once, from father to husband at the Marriage Rite, and descends to the husband’s heir. It is never sold
Temporary Darlorath | A master may convey the Darlorath of mastery over a woman for a fixed term, by written contract, to the Crown, the Church, or a private party: an indenture, a charter, a Contract Roll or Warrant, a guild or academy contract, a Hearth Training host, or a Hearth Contract. The term-holder holds her service, residence, movement, dress, correction, and conduct, and answers for her as a guardian answers. The title stays with the master, and the mastery returns to him at the term (the instruments elsewhere in this document call it mastery in trust)
What is never conveyed | Carnal use. Any carnal use by a term-holder is despoilment, and her willingness is no defense
Sublease | None. A term-holder may not lend, hire out, or assign her to any other man, house, or body
Forbidden Alienations | Sale; trade or barter; pledge or surety against a debt; stake or forfeit at wager or at arms; gift as property; bequest as goods to anyone but the lawful heir; surrender as blood-price. A term contract by her master is none of these
Penalty | Whoever sells and whoever buys is tried before the Magistracy and executed under the civil code, the buyer hanged beside the seller. The recovered woman passes by ordinary descent and no stain attaches to her
Defense | No plea of hospitality, necessity, or the woman’s assent serves. A plea of debt serves only as the ground of a petition under the Indenture Statute (Section VI)
Church censure | Separate and the Church’s own. A man tried by the Magistracy for a sale is also excommunicated under canon, and neither judgment is the other’s

changes.new_text: Settlement Outside the People

ops: The Rimborn breed true only among themselves, and no pairing with another people has produced a child. A Rimborn woman wed to a man of another people is lawfully wed and bears him nothing. The Commonwealth does not prosecute the marriage. It prosecutes everything that is not the marriage.

ops:
Matter | Rule
Lawfulness | A man of any people may petition for a Rimborn woman by Settlement. Marriage to her is lawful and no statute reaches it. Whatever is not the Rite is the heresy of the chattel
Who may petition | A citizen of good standing, Oath sworn and service completed, or a resident entered on the Registry of the Municipal Court of his March. A man with no household in the realm has no standing to petition
How | Petition to her father only, or after him her senior male kin, at the Betrothal Gathering held after Hearth Training. No bidding, no listing, no agent. A broker, factor, or go-between who carries, offers, or negotiates for a man is a trafficker
Typical Settlement | 800 to 2,000 Zarims, entered on the parish record and paid to the father through the Municipal Court. No dowry passes
Parish Record Duty | 10% of the entered Settlement, paid to the Crown through the Municipal Court at entry, on every Settlement to a man not Rimborn. Unpaid, the entry is void and the Rite is not performed. A Settlement between Rimborn households pays no duty
Childlessness | The petitioner declares before the priest that he knows the marriage will bear no child and takes it so. The declaration is entered with the Settlement. Barrenness is no ground of annulment, divorce, or dissolution, and the Canon Court does not hear it
Rite | The Marriage Rite by a Sworn Flame priest, in the realm, with the Oath-Band, the caerwevra, and the hair-lock. A covenantal marriage and no other. Without the Rite the Settlement is void and the sum is returned
Rooting | The Rite seals her to the man who holds her, whatever his people. Synchronization is kept as for any Rooted wife
Peers and entailed estates | No law forbids a peer or entailed holder to wed a Rimborn. The marriage gives no heir: the estate passes at his death by agnatic primogeniture to his nearest male kin, and her Darlorath reverts as the law directs. The stigma, not the statute, is the check
Widow | On her master’s death her Darlorath reverts to her father’s house, or to the nearest senior man of her father’s or her master’s line, to be kept or transferred again. A second transfer is a Settlement on the same rules, with the same declaration and the same duty
Leaving the realm | She crosses the border only with her master, a Magistracy exit warrant, and the Rite entry. A Rimborn woman found abroad or at the border without them is held as presumed trafficked, and the man holding her is tried for Unlawful Holding
Provenance | Her lawful standing is her parish roll: Hearth Training entered, Settlement entered, Rite entered, collar removed. An Appraiser or Constable may demand the entry. A Rimborn woman with no entry, or wearing a collar after the Rite, is held as a slaver’s girl until her parish answers for her. A Hearth-Keeper who enters a false record is tried as an accomplice to slaving
Enforcement | The Rangers carry the provenance entry in their anti-slavery manual. Rimborn men of the Guide-Companies are posted to Ranger details on the forest edge and the roads, because the Rimborn police the market that undercuts them

ops: The Commonwealth recognizes one wife to one man. The Veyrathi abolished plural households on their conversion. The Rimborn did not, and the law reaches them all the same.
changes.new_text: The Commonwealth recognizes one wife to one man. The Veyrathi abolished plural households on their conversion. The Rimborn did not, and the law reaches them all the same.

ops:
Matter | Rule
Rule | A man holds one woman by Darlorath: the woman he wed by the Rite. He holds no other
Unlawful Holding | A man who holds a woman he does not own by marriage (a second wife, a concubine, a kept woman, a ward held as a wife, a woman held by arrangement or by payment outside the Rite) commits Unlawful Holding. The penalty is execution under the civil code
The woman | She is recovered and passes by ordinary descent to her father or nearest male kin. No stain attaches to her, and her willingness is no defense for the man
Not holding | Temporary Darlorath is not holding: a Court indenture, a Crown or Church charter, Hearth Training, a Household Service Contract, and a Hearth Contract
Settlement | A Settlement outside a Rite is the heresy of the chattel, and the man who takes her under it commits Unlawful Holding besides
Plural custom | The Veyrathi abolished it at admission. The Rimborn did not, and the Commonwealth does not recognize it: a second woman held in a Rimborn hold is Unlawful Holding like any other. A Settlement buys one Rite and one wife
Prosecution | A Crown Constable investigates and the Regional Court tries it as a major criminal matter, as despoilment is tried

changes.new_text: Common Charter

ops: The Crown's women's service has one logic: a woman serves so that a man can stand in the line, and she serves under a man's call, a guardian's signature, and a Sentinel's guard. The six branches below keep that logic and use what the nine peoples' women give the realm: steadiness under a stable master, no wish to hold what they are given to keep, and hands, ears, memory and patience that the Warhost now spends men to supply.

The six branches below keep that logic and use what the nine peoples' women give the realm: steadiness under a stable master, no wish to hold what they are given to keep, and hands, ears, memory and patience that the Warhost now spends men to supply.

ops:
Matter | Rule
Status | Each branch is a Crown-chartered corps on the Contract Roll, with its own charter and its own contract, signed separately. A Thornmaiden contract does not carry over. A father who wishes his daughter to pass to another branch signs anew, and the term begins again.
Eligibility | Unmarried women of eighteen and over, Presented and veiled. A wife or widow cannot serve. Each branch names the peoples it draws on.
Contract | 24 months, renewable once, four years at most. Always signed by her father or lawful guardian, who keeps full Darlorath and may recall her at any time. The Warrant of the Ward stands on the contract's face. A contract without it is void.
Payment | 2 Zarims a month, paid up front to the father as 48 Zarims a term, and a completion bonus fixed by the branch. All coin goes to the father. The woman receives none. Recall forfeits the bonus. A recall for betrothal within six months of completion pays 6.25 Zarims for each month served.
Board | Housed and fed by the Crown in the branch's walled women's wing.
Command | A man calls the work, always. A Senior Maiden, one to each section, passes his call in the Lowered Tongue and keeps the section roll. She holds no authority over any man. No branch officer is a woman.
Conduct and correction | The Rose-Warden (one to each 250 women), the Matron of the Rose and the Sentinel of her Oath, as for the Thornmaidens. Articles IV, V and IX at all times, in the Lowered Tongue.
Casting | Only with the guardian's written consent and the Crown's authorization. Every Emberborn woman wears the training glyph, opened only to the registered phrase of the branch's Master, which the guardian delegates to him and lodges with the Bureau.
Guard | One Maidenward Oath of eight to every fifty women. A Signal Station keeps a Half-Oath of four.
Never | In an assault, in a sortie, or beyond the ground the branch names.
Dress | The Thornmaiden service dress of the ordinary women's cut, with the rose badge on the left breast and a 2 cm enamel branch bar below it. No arm-band. No dagger. A belt tool-knife serves for cord and ration.
Complaint | To a Sentinel, carried up the same day to the Rose-Warden.
Maidenward | The six branches need 1,360 more Sentinels in all. The Maidenward's authorized strength rises from 2,600 to about 4,050 (see the summary table). Each added Oath is a career post for an eight-year veteran.

ops: Magic as engineering. The Commonwealth’s particular strength is that it treats magic as a science and integrates it with engineering. Pure theory has two seats: the Arcana Scholium at Suraela, and the Maenari mage tower of Zelesti, which teaches theory in the manner of the classics. They are two options for the same thing. The Magitek Arcaneum is something else, the Commonwealth’s research-and-development engine, which teaches magic as a trade at the forge and the loom of the Duraken guildhalls, with Maenari theory supplying the design. It is a quiet symbol of why the Commonwealth, and Ironweave Works in particular, can build things like the Arcano Cannon and the paired crystal: a realm that teaches theory alone does not produce them, and a realm that teaches a trade alone does not design them.

ops: The Rimborn are 0.7% of the realm and keep no wealth beyond obligation. Their native income was the sale of daughters at the village auction. That is the Forbidden Alienation, and the Accord replaced it with the Betrothal Gathering. What remains is the Settlement, which pays once in a woman’s life and is the one line of Rimborn income that brings coin in from outside the parish, because a man of any people may petition for her (Settlement Outside the People, Section III). The Crown takes its duty on it. The Threshold Trade is what the Rimborn sell in its place: not the woman, but her labor, under the one instrument the law of Darlorath already allows. The men’s lines (the Guide-Companies, the hunt, the leather) are unchanged.

ops:
Matter | Rule
Instrument | Written in Zeylara, entered on the parish roll by the Hearth-Keeper, and stood surety for by the Rimkeeper under the Oath Triad. Names the master, the woman, the customer, the duty, the place, the term, and the rate
Contractor of record | Her master: her husband if she is married, her father if she is not. He signs, he is paid, and he answers for her as a guardian answers
Customer | The Crown, the Church, a guild, a merchant house, or a private holder
Pay | All of it to the master. She is paid nothing and holds nothing
Darlorath | Stays with the master, whole. The customer holds no mastery
Direction at work | Within the instrument’s duties any man of the customer’s house may task, question, and correct her, as any man may. His order binds her unless it contradicts her master or damages his person, household, interests, or property. She needs no Warrant of the Ward, no Matron, no Sentinel, and no collar
Outside the duties | An order outside the instrument’s duties voids the contract and fines the customer
Carnal use | None. Any carnal use is despoilment and her willingness is no defense. The contract is void at once and the customer is tried as for despoilment under mastery in trust
Sublease | None. The customer may not lend, hire out, or assign her. Doing so voids the contract and the Magistracy censures him
Recall | The master may recall her at any time. Recall ends the contract
Term | One year, renewed by the master
Synchronization | A Rooted wife serves at her master’s hold or beside him. Prolonged separation dulls the Hearthsense and the beast-reading she is hired for, and the customer buys nothing he can no longer use
Gifts | Passive gifts only are contracted. A petitioned gift is the act of a god and may be refused, so no instrument promises one
Widowhood | On her master’s death the contract lapses. Her Darlorath reverts as the law directs, and the new master signs afresh or does not
Crown | Local trade license and the contract-stamp, as on any written contract

changes.new_text: The Hearth Houses

ops: A Hearth House is a Rimborn business: a private house where Rimborn women dance Kethghal for invited men, under contract with their masters. Respectable houses of the Commonwealth find it vulgar and do not receive the men who go. It is not illegal. The Magistrals have ruled it lawful on three grounds: the venue is private, the master authorizes the woman’s performance, and what is done behind a closed door is not the Crown’s concern while no fornication is done in it. The Concordance gives it no seal, so it is no chartered guild. The Crown does not license it. The Crown taxes it.

ops:
Step | Rule
1. Founding | A Rimborn householder of good standing opens a House. He takes premises in his own name, enters the House on the parish roll under the Rimkeeper’s surety, and registers its ledger with the Treasury’s auditors. He is the House-Master
2. Contracts | He contracts with the masters of the women: a husband for his wife, a father or heir for a daughter or widow of eighteen or over. Each is a Hearth Contract for the term. The master signs, the master is paid, and the woman signs nothing
3. Direction | The master conveys temporary Darlorath over her to the House-Master for the term. He holds her service, residence, movement, dress, correction, and conduct, and answers for her as a guardian answers. The title stays with the master and the mastery returns to him at the term. Carnal use is never conveyed
4. The Evening | The women dance for guests the House-Master invites by name, behind the House’s closed door, at his direction
5. Payment | Door takings enter the ledger. The House-Master pays the Crown its duty, the parish its tithe, and each master his contracted fee, and keeps the rest

changes.new_text: The rules of the House

ops:
Matter | Rule
The door | The House’s own premises, closed and sealed: a man’s own door in law. No sign, no crier, no posting, no tout. A house that advertises is open, and the House-Master is fined as for Kethghal in the open. An inn, wayhouse, or hall that takes the public at its door is not a House, and an Evening kept there is the work of a dealing-house
Guests | Men the House-Master invites by name: citizens of good standing, or men entered on the Registry of the Municipal Court. The ledger records the head-count and the takings and never the names
Who dances | Women of eighteen and over under a master’s Hearth Contract. A woman already held by a term-holder (a Hearth Training trainee, an indentured daughter, a woman on charter) cannot be contracted, because her master has no mastery to convey while another holds it
Master’s man | A master may post a man of his house at the door for the Evening, and the House-Master may not refuse him
Guests and the women | No guest speaks to a woman, touches her, or directs her. The House-Master and his staff alone direct the dance
Carnal use | None. The fee is for the dance. Any carnal use or touch is fornication and despoilment: guest and House-Master are tried before the Regional Court, the master too if he knew, and the Magistral shuts the House. A Constable enters only on a Magistral’s warrant on a complaint of fornication. The Crown audits the ledger and never the door
Sublease | None. The House-Master may not lend, hire out, or assign a woman to another House, a guest, or any man. Doing so voids the Hearth Contract at once and returns her to her master

changes.new_text: Limits and scale

ops:
Matter | Rule
Labor pool | Rimborn wives under their husbands’ contracts, and daughters under their fathers’ in the father’s enterprise. No wife or widow serves on the Contract Roll or under indenture, and the Trade belongs to neither
Hearth Training | The trainee’s year is her host’s household labor against board and instruction. No coin passes, it is not a contract, and the Trade does not touch it
The Silence | A woman who betrays both parents loses every gift, passive and petitioned. The premium lapses with them and she serves at the ordinary women’s-trades rate
Scale | About 18,000 wives and daughters in contracted service at about 250 Zarims on average: about 4.5 million Zarims a year, about 0.05% of GDP
Crown take | Stamp and license duties on the sector run to a few hundred thousand Zarims a year
Settlement outside the people | About 700 Rimborn women reach the Betrothal Gathering each year and about 40 are petitioned by men of other peoples, at 800 to 2,000 Zarims: about 60,000 Zarims a year, and about 6,000 in Parish Record Duty. The stigma of a barren marriage keeps it small
Hearth Houses | About 60 Houses in the larger cities, each with about 8 women, about 480 women in all. A House keeps about 100 Evenings a year at about 12 guests and 12 Zarims: about 14,000 Zarims a House and about 0.85 million in all, of which about 0.26 million is the Crown’s duty, about 0.09 million the parish tithe, and about 0.3 million the masters’ fees. Each woman earns her master about 600 Zarims a year

Unification Day

ops: Unification Day is the Commonwealth’s independence day and its largest secular civic celebration. It keeps the Day of the New Oath (1780), when the Commonwealth was formed and citizenship was opened to all nine peoples, and it falls in the last week of late summer. It is the one festival the Crown proclaims and pays for; the Assembly appropriates its cost each year. It holds, in one place, the traditions of the five founding peoples: the Maenari, Satyrim, Duraken, Vykril, and Avesari. The Maestrai, Luminari, Veyrathi, and Rimborn join the shared parade, the oath-song, and the mass Circle. Unlike the Council of Tongues Day, which is kept identically by all nine peoples with no display, Unification Day is kept by tradition, each people in its own art.
